title_o: The effect of global versus local processing styles on assimilation versus contrast in social judgment.
verdict_reason: RPP data.csv (guid m65gx) has 74 rows with a discard flag; the 71 kept rows (the same rows the audit script keeps by position) carry aggressivenessScore, mapCondition and puzzleCondition, and the recomputed processing-style x prime interaction F(2,65)=0.865, p=.426, partial eta^2=.0259 matches the table.

data_files.notes: one row per participant; discard==1 for rows 16, 23, 68 (suspicion); kept cells Control 12/10, Global 15/12, Local 14/11; PID 18 appears twice (two different people: different age and gender), so unique(PID)=70 though rows=71
variable descriptions; aggressivenessScore = mean of Q5 and Q8
replicators' own script: subset(discard == 0), car::Anova type III on the same model

key_test.test: aov aggressivenessScore ~ mapCondition * puzzleCondition, car::Anova type II, key statistic = interaction

recompute.method: base R aov + drop1 on the downloaded csv (car not installed; interaction SS identical under type I/II/III here)

obstacles: audit script excludes rows by hard-coded position rather than the discard column (same result)
duplicate PID 18 makes the script's sample-size line print 70, not 71
a reply from the original authors sits on the node (Replication Project Response 2015 pdf); not opened
